## bun

```text
Bun is a fast JavaScript runtime, package manager, bundler, and test runner. (1.4.6-canary.1+3f3202e42)

Usage: bun <command> [...flags] [...args]

Commands:
  run       ./my-script.ts       Execute a file with Bun
            dev                  Run a package.json script
  test                           Run unit tests with Bun
  check                          Type check a TypeScript project
  lint                           Lint JavaScript and TypeScript, like ESLint
  fmt                            Format JavaScript and TypeScript, like Prettier
  x         bun-repl             Execute a package binary (CLI), installing if needed (bunx)
  repl                           Start a REPL session with Bun
  exec                           Run a shell script directly with Bun

  install                        Install dependencies for a package.json (bun i)
  add       hono                 Add a dependency to package.json (bun a)
  remove    is-array             Remove a dependency from package.json (bun rm)
  update    react                Update outdated dependencies
  audit                          Check installed packages for vulnerabilities
  dedupe                         Remove duplicate versions from the lockfile
  prune                          Remove packages that are not in the lockfile from node_modules
  outdated                       Display latest versions of outdated dependencies
  link      [<package>]          Register or link a local npm package
  unlink                         Unregister a local npm package
  publish                        Publish a package to the npm registry
  patch <pkg>                    Prepare a package for patching
  pm <subcommand>                Additional package management utilities
  info      lyra                 Display package metadata from the registry
  why       @remix-run/dev       Explain why a package is installed

  build     ./a.ts ./b.jsx       Bundle TypeScript & JavaScript into a single file
  compile   ./cli.ts             Compile TypeScript & JavaScript into a standalone executable

  init                           Start an empty Bun project from a built-in template
  create    astro                Create a new project from a template (bun c)
  upgrade                        Upgrade to latest version of Bun.

  <command> --help               Print help text for command.

Flags:
      --silent                        Don't print the script command
      --elide-lines=<val>             Number of lines of script output shown when using --filter (default: 0, show all lines)
  -v, --version                       Print version and exit
      --revision                      Print version with revision and exit
  -F, --filter=<val>                  Run a script in all workspace packages matching the pattern
  -b, --bun                           Force a script or package to use Bun's runtime instead of Node.js (via symlinking node)
      --no-orphans                    Exit when the parent process dies, and on exit kill every descendant.
      --shell=<val>                   Control the shell used for package.json scripts. Supports either 'bun' or 'system'
      --workspaces                    Run a script in all workspace packages (from the "workspaces" field in package.json)
      --parallel                      Run multiple scripts concurrently with Foreman-style output
      --sequential                    Run multiple scripts sequentially with Foreman-style output
      --no-exit-on-error              Continue running other scripts when one fails (with --parallel/--sequential)
      --watch                         Automatically restart the process on file change
      --watch-kill-signal=<val>       Signal whose handlers run when --watch restarts the process (default: "SIGTERM")
      --hot                           Enable auto reload in the Bun runtime, test runner, or bundler
      --no-clear-screen               Disable clearing the terminal screen on reload when --hot or --watch is enabled
      --check                         Type check before running. Nothing runs if there are type errors. Alone: bun check
      --aot                           Check the program like bun compile does, then run it with built-in objects read-only. bun test compiles it and runs the compiled code
      --aot-allow-code-from-disk      With --aot: let import() and require() load code from disk that wasn't compiled. The build takes longer
      --smol                          Use less memory, but run garbage collection more often
      --interactive                   Start a Node.js-compatible REPL, like node --interactive
  -r, --preload=<val>                 Import a module before other modules are loaded
      --require=<val>                 Alias of --preload, for Node.js compatibility
      --import=<val>                  Alias of --preload, for Node.js compatibility
      --inspect=<val>                 Activate Bun's debugger
      --inspect-wait=<val>            Activate Bun's debugger, wait for a connection before executing
      --inspect-brk=<val>             Activate Bun's debugger, set breakpoint on first line of code and wait
      --cpu-prof                      Start CPU profiler and write profile to disk on exit
      --cpu-prof-name=<val>           Specify the name of the CPU profile file
      --cpu-prof-dir=<val>            Specify the directory where the CPU profile will be saved
      --cpu-prof-md                   Output CPU profile in markdown format (grep-friendly, designed for LLM analysis)
      --cpu-prof-interval=<val>       Specify the sampling interval in microseconds for CPU profiling (default: 1000)
      --heap-prof                     Write a heap profile to disk on exit (.heapprofile)
      --heap-prof-name=<val>          Specify the name of the heap profile file
      --heap-prof-dir=<val>           Specify the directory where the heap profile will be saved
      --heap-prof-md                  Generate markdown heap profile on exit (for CLI analysis)
      --heap-prof-interval=<val>      Specify the average sampling interval in bytes for heap profiling (default: 524288)
      --if-present                    Exit without an error if the entrypoint does not exist
      --no-install                    Disable auto install in the Bun runtime
      --install=<val>                 Configure auto-install behavior. One of "auto" (default, auto-installs when no node_modules), "fallback" (missing packages only), "force" (always).
  -i                                  Auto-install dependencies during execution. Equivalent to --install=fallback.
  -e, --eval=<val>                    Evaluate argument as a script
  -p, --print=<val>                   Evaluate argument as a script and print the result
      --prefer-offline                Skip staleness checks for packages in the Bun runtime and resolve from disk
      --prefer-latest                 Use the latest matching versions of packages in the Bun runtime, always checking npm
      --port=<val>                    Set the default port for Bun.serve
      --conditions=<val>              Pass custom conditions to resolve
      --fetch-preconnect=<val>        Preconnect to a URL while code is loading
      --experimental-http2-fetch      Offer h2 in fetch() TLS ALPN. Same as BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_EXPERIMENTAL_HTTP2_CLIENT=1
      --experimental-http3-fetch      Honor Alt-Svc: h3 in fetch() and upgrade to HTTP/3. Same as BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_EXPERIMENTAL_HTTP3_CLIENT=1
      --max-http-header-size=<val>    Set the maximum size of HTTP headers in bytes. Default is 16KiB
      --insecure-http-parser          Use an insecure HTTP parser that accepts invalid HTTP headers
      --dns-result-order=<val>        Set the default order of DNS lookup results. Valid orders: verbatim (default), ipv4first, ipv6first
      --experimental-stream-iter      Enable the experimental stream/iter API (node:stream/iter, node:zlib/iter).
      --expose-gc                     Expose gc() on the global object. Has no effect on Bun.gc().
      --no-deprecation                Suppress all reporting of the custom deprecation.
      --throw-deprecation             Determine whether or not deprecation warnings result in errors.
      --no-warnings                   Silence all process warnings
      --trace-warnings                Show stack traces on process warnings
      --trace-deprecation             Show stack traces on deprecations
      --pending-deprecation           Emit pending deprecation warnings
      --redirect-warnings=<val>       Write process warnings to the given file instead of printing to stderr
      --disable-warning=<val>         Silence specific process warnings by code or type
      --title=<val>                   Set the process title
      --zero-fill-buffers             Boolean to force Buffer.allocUnsafe(size) to be zero-filled.
      --tls-min-v1.0                  Set the default TLS minimum to TLSv1.0
      --tls-min-v1.1                  Set the default TLS minimum to TLSv1.1
      --tls-min-v1.2                  Set the default TLS minimum to TLSv1.2
      --tls-min-v1.3                  Set the default TLS minimum to TLSv1.3
      --tls-max-v1.2                  Set the default TLS maximum to TLSv1.2
      --tls-max-v1.3                  Set the default TLS maximum to TLSv1.3
      --redis-preconnect              Preconnect to $REDIS_URL at startup
      --sql-preconnect                Preconnect to PostgreSQL at startup
      --no-addons                     Throw an error if process.dlopen or bun:ffi cc() is called, and disable export condition "node-addons"
      --no-ffi-cc                     Throw an error if bun:ffi cc() is called (disables the C compiler)
      --unhandled-rejections=<val>    One of "strict", "throw", "warn", "none", or "warn-with-error-code"
      --console-depth=<val>           Set the default depth for console.log object inspection (default: 2)
      --user-agent=<val>              Set the default User-Agent header for HTTP requests
      --cron-title=<val>              Title for cron execution mode
      --cron-period=<val>             Cron period for cron execution mode
      --main-fields=<val>             Main fields to lookup in package.json. Defaults to --target dependent
      --preserve-symlinks             Preserve symlinks when resolving files
      --preserve-symlinks-main        Preserve symlinks when resolving the main entry point
      --extension-order=<val>         Defaults to: .tsx,.ts,.jsx,.js,.json
      --tsconfig-override=<val>       Specify custom tsconfig.json. Default $cwd/tsconfig.json
  -d, --define=<val>                  Substitute K:V while parsing, e.g. --define process.env.NODE_ENV:"development". Values are parsed as JSON.
      --drop=<val>                    Remove function calls, e.g. --drop=console removes all console.* calls.
      --feature=<val>                 Enable a feature flag for dead-code elimination, e.g. --feature=SUPER_SECRET
  -l, --loader=<val>                  Parse files with .ext:loader, e.g. --loader .js:jsx. Valid loaders: js, jsx, ts, tsx, json, toml, text, file, wasm, napi
      --no-macros                     Disable macros from being executed in the bundler, transpiler and runtime
      --jsx-factory=<val>             Changes the function called when compiling JSX elements using the classic JSX runtime
      --jsx-fragment=<val>            Changes the function called when compiling JSX fragments
      --jsx-import-source=<val>       Declares the module specifier to be used for importing the jsx and jsxs factory functions. Default: "react"
      --jsx-runtime=<val>             "automatic" (default) or "classic"
      --jsx-side-effects              Treat JSX elements as having side effects (disable pure annotations)
      --ignore-dce-annotations        Ignore tree-shaking annotations such as @__PURE__
      --env-file=<val>                Load environment variables from the specified file(s)
      --no-env-file                   Disable automatic loading of .env files
      --cwd=<val>                     Absolute path to resolve files & entry points from. This just changes the process' cwd.
  -c, --config=<val>                  Specify path to Bun config file. Default $cwd/bunfig.toml
      --use-system-ca                 Use the system's trusted certificate authorities
      --use-openssl-ca                Use OpenSSL's default CA store instead of the bundled one
      --use-bundled-ca                Use bundled CA store
  -h, --help                          Display this menu and exit

(more flags in bun install --help, bun test --help, and bun build --help)

Learn more about Bun:            https://bun.com/docs
Join our Discord community:      https://bun.com/discord
```

## bun test

```text
Usage: bun test [flags] [<patterns>]
  Run all matching test files and print the results to stdout

Flags:
      --no-orphans                     Exit when the parent process dies, and on exit kill every descendant.
      --timeout=<val>                  Set the per-test timeout in milliseconds, default is 5000.
  -u, --update-snapshots               Update snapshot files
      --rerun-each=<val>               Re-run each test file <NUMBER> times, helps catch certain bugs
      --retry=<val>                    Default retry count for all tests, overridden by per-test { retry: N }
      --todo                           Include tests that are marked with "test.todo()"
      --only                           Run only tests that are marked with "test.only()" or "describe.only()"
      --pass-with-no-tests             Exit with code 0 when no tests are found
      --concurrent                     Treat all tests as `test.concurrent()` tests
      --randomize                      Run tests in random order
      --seed=<val>                     Set the random seed for test randomization
      --coverage                       Generate a coverage profile
      --coverage-reporter=<val>        Report coverage in 'text' and/or 'lcov'. Defaults to 'text'. Implies --coverage.
      --coverage-dir=<val>             Directory for coverage files. Defaults to 'coverage'.
      --bail=<val>                     Exit the test suite after <NUMBER> failures. If you do not specify a number, it defaults to 1.
  -t, --test-name-pattern=<val>        Run only tests with a name that matches the given regex.
      --reporter=<val>                 Test output reporter format. Available: 'junit' (requires --reporter-outfile), 'dots'. Default: console output.
      --reporter-outfile=<val>         Output file path for the reporter format (required with --reporter).
      --reporter-junit-suites=<val>    How --reporter=junit writes describe blocks: 'nested' (default) gives each block its own <testsuite>, 'flat' prefixes test names with the block names.
      --dots                           Enable dots reporter. Shorthand for --reporter=dots.
      --only-failures                  Only display test failures, hiding passing tests.
      --max-concurrency=<val>          Maximum number of concurrent tests to execute at once. Default is 20.
      --path-ignore-patterns=<val>     Glob patterns for test file paths to ignore.
      --changed=<val>                  Only run test files affected by changed files according to git. Optionally pass a commit or branch to compare against.
      --isolate=<val>                  Run each test file in a fresh global object. Leaked handles from one file cannot affect another. "modules": keep the global object and load each file's modules afresh (faster; files can see each other's changes to globals).
      --no-isolate                     With --parallel: let each worker keep one global and module registry across the files it runs (faster; files can see each other's leftovers).
      --parallel=<val>                 Run test files in parallel using N worker processes. Implies --isolate. Defaults to CPU core count.
      --parallel-delay=<val>           Milliseconds the first --parallel worker must be busy before spawning the rest. 0 spawns all immediately. Default 5.
      --test-worker                    (internal) Run as a --parallel worker, receiving files over IPC.
      --files-from=<val>               Read test file paths from a file, one per line, besides those on the command line. For lists longer than a command line may be.
      --shard=<val>                    Run a subset of test files, e.g. '--shard=1/3' runs the first of three shards. Useful for splitting tests across multiple CI jobs.
      --timings=<val>                  JSON file(s) of per-file durations (ms); several are merged, e.g. one per CI shard. Balances --shard by total time and makes --parallel start the slowest files first.
      --update-timings                 After the run, write measured per-file durations to the first --timings file (only this shard's files under --shard; merged with what was read otherwise).
      --environment=<val>              DOM for test files: 'node' (default, no DOM), 'jsdom' or 'happy-dom'. A '@vitest-environment' or '@jest-environment' comment in a file overrides it.
      --globals=<val>                  Module that 'test', 'expect' and the other globals come from: 'bun' (default) uses "vitest" in files that import from it and "bun:test" elsewhere, 'vitest' uses it everywhere.
      --react-compiler                 Compile components and hooks with the React Compiler. Test files, preloads and node_modules are left alone
      --no-compile-function-source     With --aot: don't embed function source code. fn.toString() returns [native code]

Examples:
  Run all test files
  bun test

  Run all test files with "foo" or "bar" in the file name
  bun test foo bar

  Run all test files, only including tests whose names includes "baz"
  bun test --test-name-pattern baz

  Type check the test files and what they import, then run them
  bun test --check

  Compile the test files ahead of time, then run them
  bun test --aot

Full documentation is available at https://bun.com/docs/cli/test
```

## bun check

```text
Usage: bun check [flags] [...files or directories]
  Type check a TypeScript project.

  Uses the nearest tsconfig.json and reports the same errors as tsc, using all CPU cores.
  Pass files or directories to check only those and their imports.
  Project references are followed, like tsc -b, and nothing has to be built first.

Flags:
  -p, --project=<val>        Path to a tsconfig.json or its directory
      --pretty=<val>         Show source code around each error (default in a terminal)
  -b, --build                Check the projects in references too, like tsc -b
      --no-pretty            One line per error, like tsc --pretty false (default when piped)
      --all                  Show every error (above 50, identical errors are grouped)
      --threads=<val>        Number of threads (default: one per CPU core)
      --no-follow-imports    Report only the errors of the files you name, not of the files they import
      --timing               Print load and check times, and the slowest files
      --aot                  Also report the errors bun compile would report for these entry points
      --explain=<val>        With --aot: list the code that would compile to a slow path and how to fix it, worst first. Other reports: guards, json, trim
      --define=<val>         With --aot: substitute k with v while parsing, like bun compile --define
      --cwd=<val>            Set the working directory
      --no-script            Run the type checker even if the project has a check script
  -h, --help                 Print this help menu
      --strict, --target=<val>, ...  Any compiler option, as for tsc. Overrides tsconfig.json

Examples:
  Check the current project
  bun check

  Check one file and everything it imports
  bun check src/index.ts

  Check another project
  bun check -p packages/server

  Try a stricter option without editing tsconfig.json
  bun check --noUncheckedIndexedAccess

  Check a file, then run it
  bun --check src/index.ts

  Also report the errors bun compile would report
  bun check --aot src/index.ts

Full documentation is available at https://bun.com/docs/runtime/check
```

## bun lint

```text
Usage: bun lint [flags] [...files, directories or patterns]
  Find and fix problems in JavaScript and TypeScript.

Flags:
      --fix                   Fix problems and write the files
      --staged                Only lint files that are staged in git
      --changed=<val>         Only lint files that differ from a branch or commit (default: the default branch)
      --rule=<val>            Set a rule, or turn off a plugin: --rule 'eqeqeq: [error, smart]', --rule 'unicorn/*: off'
      --rules                 List the built-in rules
      --explain=<val>         Print the documentation of a rule
      --type-aware            Also run the rules that need types
      --quiet                 Report errors only
      --max-warnings=<val>    Exit with 1 if there are more warnings than this
      --init                  Add a [lint] section to bunfig.toml
      --doctor                Show which rules run natively and which packages you can remove
      --no-script             Run the linter even if the project has a lint script

Examples:
  bun lint
  bun lint --fix src
  bun lint --rule 'no-console: error'

Full documentation is available at https://bun.com/docs/lint
See every flag with bun lint --help --all
```

## bun fmt

```text
Usage: bun fmt [flags] [...files, directories or patterns]
  Format JavaScript, TypeScript, CSS, HTML, JSON, YAML, Markdown and more.

Flags:
  -c, --check                   Do not write. Exit with 1 if a file needs formatting
      --staged                  Only format files that are staged in git, and stage them again
      --changed=<val>           Only format files that differ from a branch or commit (default: the default branch)
      --stdin-filepath=<val>    Format standard input as this file and print the result
      --print-width=<val>       The line length to wrap at (default: 80)
      --use-tabs                Indent with tabs
      --no-semi                 Only print semicolons where they are needed
      --single-quote            Use single quotes
      --init                    Add a [fmt] section to bunfig.toml
      --doctor                  Show which files are formatted natively and which packages you can remove
      --no-script               Run the formatter even if the project has a fmt script

Examples:
  bun fmt
  bun fmt src test/a.test.ts
  bun fmt --check

Full documentation is available at https://bun.com/docs/format
See every flag with bun fmt --help --all
```

## bun repl

```text
Usage: bun run [flags] <file or script>

Flags:
      --silent                        Don't print the script command
      --elide-lines=<val>             Number of lines of script output shown when using --filter (default: 0, show all lines)
  -F, --filter=<val>                  Run a script in all workspace packages matching the pattern
  -b, --bun                           Force a script or package to use Bun's runtime instead of Node.js (via symlinking node)
      --no-orphans                    Exit when the parent process dies, and on exit kill every descendant.
      --shell=<val>                   Control the shell used for package.json scripts. Supports either 'bun' or 'system'
      --workspaces                    Run a script in all workspace packages (from the "workspaces" field in package.json)
      --parallel                      Run multiple scripts concurrently with Foreman-style output
      --sequential                    Run multiple scripts sequentially with Foreman-style output
      --no-exit-on-error              Continue running other scripts when one fails (with --parallel/--sequential)
      --watch                         Automatically restart the process on file change
      --watch-kill-signal=<val>       Signal whose handlers run when --watch restarts the process (default: "SIGTERM")
      --hot                           Enable auto reload in the Bun runtime, test runner, or bundler
      --no-clear-screen               Disable clearing the terminal screen on reload when --hot or --watch is enabled
      --check                         Type check before running. Nothing runs if there are type errors. Alone: bun check
      --aot                           Check the program like bun compile does, then run it with built-in objects read-only. bun test compiles it and runs the compiled code
      --aot-allow-code-from-disk      With --aot: let import() and require() load code from disk that wasn't compiled. The build takes longer
      --smol                          Use less memory, but run garbage collection more often
      --interactive                   Start a Node.js-compatible REPL, like node --interactive
  -r, --preload=<val>                 Import a module before other modules are loaded
      --require=<val>                 Alias of --preload, for Node.js compatibility
      --import=<val>                  Alias of --preload, for Node.js compatibility
      --inspect=<val>                 Activate Bun's debugger
      --inspect-wait=<val>            Activate Bun's debugger, wait for a connection before executing
      --inspect-brk=<val>             Activate Bun's debugger, set breakpoint on first line of code and wait
      --cpu-prof                      Start CPU profiler and write profile to disk on exit
      --cpu-prof-name=<val>           Specify the name of the CPU profile file
      --cpu-prof-dir=<val>            Specify the directory where the CPU profile will be saved
      --cpu-prof-md                   Output CPU profile in markdown format (grep-friendly, designed for LLM analysis)
      --cpu-prof-interval=<val>       Specify the sampling interval in microseconds for CPU profiling (default: 1000)
      --heap-prof                     Write a heap profile to disk on exit (.heapprofile)
      --heap-prof-name=<val>          Specify the name of the heap profile file
      --heap-prof-dir=<val>           Specify the directory where the heap profile will be saved
      --heap-prof-md                  Generate markdown heap profile on exit (for CLI analysis)
      --heap-prof-interval=<val>      Specify the average sampling interval in bytes for heap profiling (default: 524288)
      --if-present                    Exit without an error if the entrypoint does not exist
      --no-install                    Disable auto install in the Bun runtime
      --install=<val>                 Configure auto-install behavior. One of "auto" (default, auto-installs when no node_modules), "fallback" (missing packages only), "force" (always).
  -i                                  Auto-install dependencies during execution. Equivalent to --install=fallback.
  -e, --eval=<val>                    Evaluate argument as a script
  -p, --print=<val>                   Evaluate argument as a script and print the result
      --prefer-offline                Skip staleness checks for packages in the Bun runtime and resolve from disk
      --prefer-latest                 Use the latest matching versions of packages in the Bun runtime, always checking npm
      --port=<val>                    Set the default port for Bun.serve
      --conditions=<val>              Pass custom conditions to resolve
      --fetch-preconnect=<val>        Preconnect to a URL while code is loading
      --experimental-http2-fetch      Offer h2 in fetch() TLS ALPN. Same as BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_EXPERIMENTAL_HTTP2_CLIENT=1
      --experimental-http3-fetch      Honor Alt-Svc: h3 in fetch() and upgrade to HTTP/3. Same as BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_EXPERIMENTAL_HTTP3_CLIENT=1
      --max-http-header-size=<val>    Set the maximum size of HTTP headers in bytes. Default is 16KiB
      --insecure-http-parser          Use an insecure HTTP parser that accepts invalid HTTP headers
      --dns-result-order=<val>        Set the default order of DNS lookup results. Valid orders: verbatim (default), ipv4first, ipv6first
      --experimental-stream-iter      Enable the experimental stream/iter API (node:stream/iter, node:zlib/iter).
      --expose-gc                     Expose gc() on the global object. Has no effect on Bun.gc().
      --no-deprecation                Suppress all reporting of the custom deprecation.
      --throw-deprecation             Determine whether or not deprecation warnings result in errors.
      --no-warnings                   Silence all process warnings
      --trace-warnings                Show stack traces on process warnings
      --trace-deprecation             Show stack traces on deprecations
      --pending-deprecation           Emit pending deprecation warnings
      --redirect-warnings=<val>       Write process warnings to the given file instead of printing to stderr
      --disable-warning=<val>         Silence specific process warnings by code or type
      --title=<val>                   Set the process title
      --zero-fill-buffers             Boolean to force Buffer.allocUnsafe(size) to be zero-filled.
      --tls-min-v1.0                  Set the default TLS minimum to TLSv1.0
      --tls-min-v1.1                  Set the default TLS minimum to TLSv1.1
      --tls-min-v1.2                  Set the default TLS minimum to TLSv1.2
      --tls-min-v1.3                  Set the default TLS minimum to TLSv1.3
      --tls-max-v1.2                  Set the default TLS maximum to TLSv1.2
      --tls-max-v1.3                  Set the default TLS maximum to TLSv1.3
      --redis-preconnect              Preconnect to $REDIS_URL at startup
      --sql-preconnect                Preconnect to PostgreSQL at startup
      --no-addons                     Throw an error if process.dlopen or bun:ffi cc() is called, and disable export condition "node-addons"
      --no-ffi-cc                     Throw an error if bun:ffi cc() is called (disables the C compiler)
      --unhandled-rejections=<val>    One of "strict", "throw", "warn", "none", or "warn-with-error-code"
      --console-depth=<val>           Set the default depth for console.log object inspection (default: 2)
      --user-agent=<val>              Set the default User-Agent header for HTTP requests
      --cron-title=<val>              Title for cron execution mode
      --cron-period=<val>             Cron period for cron execution mode
      --main-fields=<val>             Main fields to lookup in package.json. Defaults to --target dependent
      --preserve-symlinks             Preserve symlinks when resolving files
      --preserve-symlinks-main        Preserve symlinks when resolving the main entry point
      --extension-order=<val>         Defaults to: .tsx,.ts,.jsx,.js,.json
      --tsconfig-override=<val>       Specify custom tsconfig.json. Default $cwd/tsconfig.json
  -d, --define=<val>                  Substitute K:V while parsing, e.g. --define process.env.NODE_ENV:"development". Values are parsed as JSON.
      --drop=<val>                    Remove function calls, e.g. --drop=console removes all console.* calls.
      --feature=<val>                 Enable a feature flag for dead-code elimination, e.g. --feature=SUPER_SECRET
  -l, --loader=<val>                  Parse files with .ext:loader, e.g. --loader .js:jsx. Valid loaders: js, jsx, ts, tsx, json, toml, text, file, wasm, napi
      --no-macros                     Disable macros from being executed in the bundler, transpiler and runtime
      --jsx-factory=<val>             Changes the function called when compiling JSX elements using the classic JSX runtime
      --jsx-fragment=<val>            Changes the function called when compiling JSX fragments
      --jsx-import-source=<val>       Declares the module specifier to be used for importing the jsx and jsxs factory functions. Default: "react"
      --jsx-runtime=<val>             "automatic" (default) or "classic"
      --jsx-side-effects              Treat JSX elements as having side effects (disable pure annotations)
      --ignore-dce-annotations        Ignore tree-shaking annotations such as @__PURE__
      --env-file=<val>                Load environment variables from the specified file(s)
      --no-env-file                   Disable automatic loading of .env files
      --cwd=<val>                     Absolute path to resolve files & entry points from. This just changes the process' cwd.
  -c, --config=<val>                  Specify path to Bun config file. Default $cwd/bunfig.toml
      --use-system-ca                 Use the system's trusted certificate authorities
      --use-openssl-ca                Use OpenSSL's default CA store instead of the bundled one
      --use-bundled-ca                Use bundled CA store
  -h, --help                          Display this menu and exit

Examples:
  Run a JavaScript or TypeScript file
  bun run ./index.js
  bun run ./index.tsx

  Run a package.json script
  bun run dev
  bun run lint

Full documentation is available at https://bun.com/docs/cli/run
```

## bun install

```text
Usage: bun install [flags] <name>@<version>
Alias: bun i

  Install the dependencies listed in package.json.

Flags:
  -c, --config=<val>                          Specify path to config file (bunfig.toml)
  -y, --yarn                                  Write a yarn.lock file (yarn v1)
  -p, --production                            Don't install devDependencies
      --no-save                               Don't update package.json or save a lockfile
      --save                                  Save to package.json (true by default)
      --ca=<val>                              Provide a Certificate Authority signing certificate
      --cafile=<val>                          The same as `--ca`, but is a file path to the certificate
      --dry-run                               Perform a dry run without making changes
      --frozen-lockfile                       Disallow changes to lockfile
  -f, --force                                 Always request the latest versions from the registry & reinstall all dependencies
      --cache-dir=<val>                       Store & load cached data from a specific directory path
      --no-cache                              Ignore manifest cache entirely
      --silent                                Don't log anything
      --quiet                                 Only show tarball name when packing
      --verbose                               Excessively verbose logging
      --no-progress                           Disable the progress bar
      --no-summary                            Don't print a summary
      --no-verify                             Skip verifying integrity of newly downloaded packages
      --offline                               Never touch the network: resolve and install only from the local cache
      --prefer-offline                        Use cached package metadata regardless of age; only fetch what is missing
      --ignore-scripts                        Skip lifecycle scripts for all packages, including the project's package.json and trusted dependencies
      --trust                                 Add to trustedDependencies in the project's package.json and install the package(s)
  -g, --global                                Install globally
      --cwd=<val>                             Set a specific cwd
      --env-file=<val>                        Load environment variables from the specified file(s)
      --no-env-file                           Disable automatic loading of .env files
      --backend=<val>                         Platform-specific optimizations for installing dependencies. Possible values: "hardlink" (default), "symlink", "copyfile"
      --registry=<val>                        Use a specific registry by default, overriding .npmrc, bunfig.toml and environment variables
      --concurrent-scripts=<val>              Maximum number of concurrent jobs for lifecycle scripts (default: 2x CPU cores)
      --network-concurrency=<val>             Maximum number of concurrent network requests (default 64)
      --save-text-lockfile                    Save a text-based lockfile
      --omit=<val>                            Exclude 'dev', 'optional', or 'peer' dependencies from install
      --lockfile-only                         Generate a lockfile without installing dependencies
      --linker=<val>                          Linker strategy (one of "isolated" or "hoisted")
      --minimum-release-age=<val>             Only install packages published at least N seconds ago (security feature)
      --minimum-release-age-excludes=<val>    Packages exempt from --minimum-release-age (comma-separated or repeated; replaces the bunfig.toml list)
      --cpu=<val>                             Override CPU architecture for optional dependencies (e.g., x64, arm64, * for all)
      --os=<val>                              Override operating system for optional dependencies (e.g., linux, darwin, * for all)
      --libc=<val>                            Override libc for optional dependencies (e.g., glibc, musl, * for all)
      --use-system-ca                         Use the system's trusted certificate authorities
      --use-openssl-ca                        Use OpenSSL's default CA store instead of the bundled one
      --use-bundled-ca                        Use bundled CA store
  -h, --help                                  Print this help menu
  -d, --dev                                   Add dependency to "devDependencies"
      --optional                              Add dependency to "optionalDependencies"
      --peer                                  Add dependency to "peerDependencies"
      --save-prod                             Add dependency to "dependencies", also when another group lists it
  -E, --exact                                 Add the exact version instead of the ^range
  -F, --filter=<val>                          Install packages for the matching workspaces
  -a, --analyze                               Analyze & install all dependencies of files passed as arguments recursively (using Bun's bundler)
      --only-missing                          Only add dependencies to package.json if they are not already present
      --catalog=<val>                         Add the resolved version to the root package.json catalog and depend on it as "catalog:" (use --catalog=NAME for a named catalog)

Examples:
  Install the dependencies for the current project
  bun install

  Skip devDependencies
  bun install --production

Full documentation is available at https://bun.com/docs/cli/install.
```

## bun update

```text
Usage: bun update [flags] <name>@<version>
Alias: bun up

Flags:

  -p, --production                            Only update dependencies and optionalDependencies (alias: --prod)
      --no-save                               Don't update package.json or save a lockfile
      --save                                  Save to package.json (true by default)
      --ca=<val>                              Provide a Certificate Authority signing certificate
      --cafile=<val>                          The same as `--ca`, but is a file path to the certificate

      --prefer-offline                        Use cached package metadata regardless of age; only fetch what is missing
      --ignore-scripts                        Skip lifecycle scripts for all packages, including the project's package.json and trusted dependencies
      --trust                                 Add to trustedDependencies in the project's package.json and install the package(s)
  -g, --global                                Install globally
      --cwd=<val>                             Set a specific cwd
      --env-file=<val>                        Load environment variables from the specified file(s)
      --no-env-file                           Disable automatic loading of .env files
      --backend=<val>                         Platform-specific optimizations for installing dependencies. Possible values: "hardlink" (default), "symlink", "copyfile"
      --registry=<val>                        Use a specific registry by default, overriding .npmrc, bunfig.toml and environment variables
      --concurrent-scripts=<val>              Maximum number of concurrent jobs for lifecycle scripts (default: 2x CPU cores)
      --network-concurrency=<val>             Maximum number of concurrent network requests (default 64)
      --save-text-lockfile                    Save a text-based lockfile
      --omit=<val>                            Exclude 'dev', 'optional', or 'peer' dependencies from install
      --lockfile-only                         Generate a lockfile without installing dependencies
      --linker=<val>                          Linker strategy (one of "isolated" or "hoisted")
      --minimum-release-age=<val>             Only install packages published at least N seconds ago (security feature)
      --minimum-release-age-excludes=<val>    Packages exempt from --minimum-release-age (comma-separated or repeated; replaces the bunfig.toml list)
      --cpu=<val>                             Override CPU architecture for optional dependencies (e.g., x64, arm64, * for all)
      --os=<val>                              Override operating system for optional dependencies (e.g., linux, darwin, * for all)
      --libc=<val>                            Override libc for optional dependencies (e.g., glibc, musl, * for all)

      --use-openssl-ca                        Use OpenSSL's default CA store instead of the bundled one

  -h, --help                                  Print this help menu
  -L, --latest                                Update packages to their latest versions, ignoring the ranges in package.json
  -i, --interactive                           Show an interactive list of outdated packages to select for update
  -F, --filter=<val>                          Update packages for the matching workspaces
  -r, --recursive                             Update packages in all workspaces
  -d, --dev                                   Only update devDependencies
      --no-optional                           Don't update optionalDependencies
      --depth=<val>                           Only 0 is accepted: update direct dependencies and keep transitive dependencies at their locked versions
  -E, --exact                                 Write exact versions to package.json instead of ^ or ~ ranges

  Update every @types package, or everything except webpack:
  bun update '@types/*'
  bun update '!webpack'

  Only update devDependencies:
  bun update --dev

  Only update dependencies and optionalDependencies:
  bun update --prod

  Only update direct dependencies, keep transitive dependencies locked:
  bun update --depth 0

Full documentation is available at https://bun.com/docs/cli/update.
```

## bun audit

```text
Usage: bun audit [flags]

  Check installed packages for vulnerabilities.
  bun audit fix upgrades vulnerable packages to the lowest safe version that still satisfies every dependent's range.

Flags:
      --audit-level=<val>    Only print advisories with severity greater than or equal to <level> (low, moderate, high, critical)
  -p, --production           Skip packages that are only needed by devDependencies (alias: --prod)
      --omit=<val>           Skip packages that are only needed by the given dependency types: dev, optional, or peer (repeatable)
      --ignore=<val>         Ignore advisories by GHSA or numeric advisory ID (repeatable)
      --json                 Output in JSON format
      --dry-run              Show what bun audit fix would change without changing anything
  -L, --latest               Also apply fixes your declared ranges exclude, rewriting package.json
      --cwd=<val>            Set a specific cwd
  -h, --help                 Print this help menu

Examples:
  Check the current project's packages for vulnerabilities.
  bun audit

  Output package vulnerabilities in JSON format.
  bun audit --json

  Upgrade vulnerable packages in bun.lock and node_modules; package.json is only changed when an exact pin has to be bumped.
  bun audit fix

  Show what bun audit fix would change without changing anything.
  bun audit fix --dry-run

  Also apply fixes that your package.json ranges exclude, rewriting those ranges.
  bun audit fix --latest

Full documentation is available at https://bun.com/docs/install/audit.
```

## bun dedupe

```text
Usage: bun dedupe [flags]

  Remove duplicate versions from bun.lock by re-resolving dependency ranges onto versions that are already in the lockfile, then install.

Flags:
      --check              Exit with code 1 if the lockfile has duplicate versions that can be removed, without changing anything
      --dry-run            Print the duplicate versions that would be removed without changing anything
      --lockfile-only      Rewrite bun.lock without installing
      --frozen-lockfile    Fail instead of rewriting bun.lock when duplicate versions can be removed
      --linker=<val>       Install with the given linker (one of "isolated" or "hoisted")
      --silent             Don't log anything
      --cwd=<val>          Set a specific cwd
  -h, --help               Print this help menu

Examples:
  Remove duplicate versions and install
  bun dedupe

  Only report removable duplicates; exit code 1 if there are any (for CI)
  bun dedupe --check

  Show what would be removed without changing anything
  bun dedupe --dry-run

  Rewrite bun.lock without installing
  bun dedupe --lockfile-only

Full documentation is available at https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/dedupe.
```

## bun prune

```text
Usage: bun prune [flags]

  Remove packages from node_modules that are not in bun.lock. With --production, also remove packages that are only needed by devDependencies.

Flags:
  -p, --production      Also remove packages that are only needed by devDependencies (alias: --prod)
      --omit=<val>      Also remove packages that are only needed by the given dependency types
      --check           Exit with code 1 if node_modules has packages that can be removed, without deleting anything
      --dry-run         Print what would be removed without deleting anything
      --os=<val>        Prune for a different operating system than the current one
      --cpu=<val>       Prune for a different CPU architecture than the current one
      --libc=<val>      Prune for a different libc than the current one
      --linker=<val>    Linker to assume when node_modules mixes isolated and hoisted installs (one of "isolated" or "hoisted")
  -F, --filter=<val>    Only prune the node_modules folders of the matching workspaces
      --silent          Don't log anything
      --cwd=<val>       Set a specific cwd
  -h, --help            Print this help menu

Examples:
  Remove packages that are not in bun.lock from node_modules
  bun prune

  Also remove devDependencies, e.g. after the build step in a Dockerfile
  bun prune --production

  Show what would be removed without deleting anything
  bun prune --dry-run

  Only report what would be removed; exit code 1 if there is anything (for CI)
  bun prune --check

  Only prune what the app workspace no longer needs
  bun prune --production --filter app

Full documentation is available at https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/prune.
```

```text
      --aot-huge-heap                                  With --aot: remove the 32 GB heap limit per thread. Uses more memory and runs slower
      --no-compile-function-source                     With --aot: don't embed function source code. fn.toString() returns [native code]
      --compile-in-place                               With --aot: keep modules at their paths on disk and load anything that wasn't compiled from there. The executable only runs on the machine that built it

      --aot-allow-code-from-disk                       With --aot: let import(), require() and new Worker() load code that isn't in the executable from disk at run time. Makes it larger and slower
      --aot-harden=<val>                               With --aot: make a bug in the compiler harder to turn into a memory bug. Takes proof-checks, ignore-told-ranges. Runs slower

      --aot-order=<val>                                With --aot: lay code and data out by order file(s) that runs of an executable built by --aot-record-order wrote; comma-separated or repeated, most important first

      --bytecode                                       Use a bytecode cache

      --sourcemap=<val>                                Build with sourcemaps - 'linked', 'inline', 'external', or 'none'
      --banner=<val>                                   Add a banner to the bundled output such as "use client"; for a bundle being used with RSCs
      --footer=<val>                                   Add a footer to the bundled output such as // built with bun!
      --format=<val>                                   Specifies the module format to build to. "esm", "cjs" and "iife" are supported. Defaults to "esm", or "cjs" with --bytecode.
      --root=<val>                                     Root directory used for multiple entry points
      --splitting                                      Enable code splitting
      --no-split-require                               With --splitting and --target bun: keep a require()'d ESM file in the calling chunk instead of emitting a chunk loaded at the call
      --no-module-preload                              With --splitting and --target browser: don't emit  for the chunks an entry or import() loads
      --min-chunk-size=<val>                           With --splitting, also fold side-effect-free chunks smaller than this many source bytes into a chunk more entry points load. Default: 0 (off); 16384 is a good value for browser builds
      --public-path=<val>                              A prefix to be appended to any import paths in bundled code
  -e, --external=<val>                                 Exclude module from transpilation (can use * wildcards). ex: -e react

      --reject-unresolved                              Fail the build on any dynamic import()/require() specifier that cannot be resolved at build time.
      --packages=<val>                                 Add dependencies to bundle or keep them external. "external", "bundle" is supported. Defaults to "bundle".
      --entry-naming=<val>                             Customize entry point filenames. Defaults to "[dir]/[name].[ext]"
      --chunk-naming=<val>                             Customize chunk filenames. Defaults to "[name]-[hash].[ext]"
      --asset-naming=<val>                             Customize asset filenames. Defaults to "[name]-[hash].[ext]"
      --react-fast-refresh                             Enable React Fast Refresh transform (does not emit hot-module code, use this for testing)
      --react-compiler                                 Enable the React Compiler optimizing transform
      --no-bundle                                      Transpile file only, do not bundle
      --check                                          Type check the entry points and what they import. Nothing is bundled if there are type errors
      --dts                                            Write declaration files (.d.ts), and each output file with its types kept (.aot.ts), to --outdir. Implies --check
      --emit-dce-annotations                           Re-emit DCE annotations in bundles. Enabled by default unless --minify-whitespace is passed.
      --no-deprecated-namespace-object-setters         Make bundled module namespace objects getter-only (the default in a future release)
      --minify                                         Enable all minification flags
      --minify-syntax                                  Minify syntax and inline data
      --minify-whitespace                              Minify whitespace
      --minify-identifiers                             Minify identifiers
      --keep-names                                     Preserve original function and class names when minifying
      --css-chunking                                   Chunk CSS files together to reduce duplicated CSS loaded in a browser. Only has an effect when multiple entrypoints import CSS
      --conditions=<val>                               Pass custom conditions to resolve
      --app                                            (EXPERIMENTAL) Build a web app for production using Bun Bake.
      --env=<val>                                      Inline environment variables into the bundle as process.env.${name}. Defaults to 'disable'. To inline environment variables matching a prefix, use my prefix like 'FOO_PUBLIC_*'.
      --windows-hide-console                           When using --compile targeting Windows, prevent a Command prompt from opening alongside the executable
      --windows-icon=<val>                             When using --compile targeting Windows, assign an executable icon
      --windows-title=<val>                            When using --compile targeting Windows, set the executable product name
      --windows-publisher=<val>                        When using --compile targeting Windows, set the executable company name
      --windows-version=<val>                          When using --compile targeting Windows, set the executable version (e.g. 1.2.3.4)
      --windows-description=<val>                      When using --compile targeting Windows, set the executable description
      --windows-copyright=<val>                        When using --compile targeting Windows, set the executable copyright
      --debug-dump-server-files                        When --app is set, dump all server files to disk even when building statically
      --debug-no-minify                                When --app is set, do not minify anything

Examples:
  Frontend web apps:
  bun build --outfile=bundle.js ./src/index.ts
  bun build --minify --splitting --outdir=out ./index.jsx ./lib/worker.ts

  Bundle code to be run in Bun (reduces server startup time)
  bun build --target=bun --outfile=server.js ./server.ts

  Creating a standalone executable (see https://bun.com/docs/compiler/executables)
  bun build --compile --outfile=my-app ./cli.ts

A full list of flags is available at https://bun.com/docs/bundler
```

## bun compile

```text
Usage: bun compile [flags] [<entrypoint>]
  Compile TypeScript & JavaScript into a standalone executable, ahead of time.

  Short for bun build --compile --aot. Without an entry point, it compiles the file that "bin" in

  The entry point can be the name of an executable of an installed package, as in bun run.

      --preserve-symlinks-main                         Preserve symlinks when resolving the main entry point
      --extension-order=<val>                          Defaults to: .tsx,.ts,.jsx,.js,.json
      --tsconfig-override=<val>                        Specify custom tsconfig.json. Default $cwd/tsconfig.json
  -d, --define=<val>                                   Substitute K:V while parsing, e.g. --define process.env.NODE_ENV:"development". Values are parsed as JSON.
      --drop=<val>                                     Remove function calls, e.g. --drop=console removes all console.* calls.
      --feature=<val>                                  Enable a feature flag for dead-code elimination, e.g. --feature=SUPER_SECRET
  -l, --loader=<val>                                   Parse files with .ext:loader, e.g. --loader .js:jsx. Valid loaders: js, jsx, ts, tsx, json, toml, text, file, wasm, napi
      --no-macros                                      Disable macros from being executed in the bundler, transpiler and runtime

Examples:
  Compile a program into a standalone executable
  bun compile ./cli.ts

  Choose the name of the executable

  Compile the command-line tool of an installed package

  List the code that compiled to a slow path
```

## bun init

```text
Usage: bun init [flags] [<folder>]
  Initialize a Bun project in the current directory.
  Creates a package.json, tsconfig.json, and bunfig.toml if they don't exist.

Flags:
      --help             Print this menu
  -y, --yes              Accept all default options
  -m, --minimal          Only initialize type definitions
  -r, --react            Initialize a React project
      --react=tailwind   Initialize a React project with TailwindCSS
      --react=shadcn     Initialize a React project with @shadcn/ui and TailwindCSS
      --use-system-ca    Use the system's trusted certificate authorities during installation
      --use-openssl-ca   Use OpenSSL's default CA store instead of the bundled one during installation
      --use-bundled-ca   Use bundled CA store during installation

Examples:
  bun init
  bun init --yes
  bun init --react
  bun init --react=tailwind my-app
```

## bun create

```text
Usage:
  bun create <MyReactComponent.(jsx|tsx)>
  bun create <template> [...flags] dest
  bun create <github-org/repo> [...flags] dest

Environment variables:
  GITHUB_TOKEN         Supply a token to download code from GitHub with a higher rate limit
  GITHUB_API_DOMAIN    Configure custom/enterprise GitHub domain. Default "api.github.com"
  NPM_CLIENT           Absolute path to the npm client executable
  BUN_CREATE_DIR       Custom path for global templates (default: $HOME/.bun-create)

React Component Projects:
  • Turn an existing React component into a complete frontend dev environment
  • Automatically starts a hot-reloading dev server
  • Auto-detects & configures TailwindCSS and shadcn/ui

  bun create <MyReactComponent.(jsx|tsx)>

Templates:
  • NPM: Runs bunx create-<template> with given arguments
  • GitHub: Downloads repository contents as template
  • Local: Uses templates from $HOME/.bun-create/<name> or ./.bun-create/<name>

Learn more: https://bun.com/docs/cli/bun-create
```

## bun upgrade

```text
Usage: bun upgrade [flags]
  Upgrade Bun

Examples:
  Install the latest canary version
  bun upgrade

  Switch from the canary version back to the latest stable release
  bun upgrade --stable

Full documentation is available at https://bun.com/docs/installation#upgrading
```
